NORTH‑WEST FRONTIER
PROVINCE FOODSTUFFS (DISPOSAL AND REWARD) RULES, 1972
[Gazette of N: W. F. P., Part
I, 22nd December 1972]
No. 8751/G‑368.‑In pursuance of the
provisions contained fn section 6‑A of the West Pakistan Foodstuffs
(Control) Act, 1958 (W. P. Act No. XX of 1958), the Governor of the North‑West
Frontier Province, is pleased to make the following rules, namely :‑
1. Short title,
extent and commencement.‑(1) These rules may be called the North‑West
Frontier Province Foodstuffs (Disposal and Reward) Rules, 1972.
(2) They shall extend to the
whole of the North‑West Frontier Province, except the Tribal Areas.
(3) They shall come Into force
at once.
2. Definitions.‑In these
rules, unless the context otherwise requires, the following expressions shall
have the meanings hereby respectively
assigned to them, that is to
say‑
(a) "Act" means the West Pakistan Foodstuffs (Control)
Act, 1958;
(b) "District Food Controller" or
"Rationing Controller" means the District Food Controller or the
Rationing Controller of the Food Department;
(c) "Government" means the Government of
the North‑West Frontier Province; and
(d) "notified order" means an order notified under
section 3 of the Act.
3. Disposal of
forfeited foodstuff:‑(1) Any foodstuff forfeited to Government under
the provisions of the Act or notified order shall be handed over for disposal
to the District Food Controller or the Rationing Controller of the District
concerned.
(2) District Food Controller or the Rationing
Controller to whom the foodstuff is handed over under sub‑rule (1) shall
dispose it of‑
(i) if the forfeited commodity is of standard quality
and is not in deteriorated condition through the authorised dealer or a
rationing depot holder in such manner and at such rate as may, from time to
time, be prescribed by the competent authority;
(ii) if the forfeited commodity is not of a standard
quality or is in a deteriorated condition, by auction after first obtaining
permission from the competent authority.
(3) The proceeds of sale or auction, as the case may
be, of the forfeited commodity shall be credited into Government Treasury under
the Head "XLVI‑Miscellaneous, etc. Provincial".
4, Reward to
informer.‑‑(1) In a case, whether ending in conviction or not,
in which the food‑stuff has been forfeited to Government, the Court
trying the offence may order payment of a reward not exceeding one‑fourth
in value of the quantity confiscated to the person or persons responsible for
the detection of the case.
(2) The District Food Controller or the Rationing
Controller shall pay reward to such person or persons, in accordance with the
order made by the trying Court under sub‑rule (1).
